title: 3.8.10 Lab: Round-Trip an Object Through JSON
description: Save an object to JSON text, restore it with JSON.parse, and prove the restored copy is independent of the original. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create an object
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it player; use any name that fits) holding an object with at least two properties, one of them a number.

steps.title: Save it to text
steps.instructions: Use JSON.stringify to turn player into a string, and store that string in a variable (the lesson calls it saved).

steps.title: Restore it
steps.instructions: Use JSON.parse on saved to build a new variable (the lesson calls it restored) back into a usable object.

steps.title: Prove it works
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print a number property of the restored object plus one, and print one of the original properties. Confirm the restored value behaves like a real object.

requirements.title: Object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Declare an object in braces (the lesson calls it player) with at least two properties, one of them a number.

requirements.title: Saved with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify to produce text. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: JSON.stringify(player) turns the object into text. Keep that text in a variable.

requirements.title: Restored with parse
requirements.description: Calls JSON.parse on the saved text. Help: 3.8.8 (JSON.parse — Text Back to Object)
requirements.hint: JSON.parse(saved) turns the text back into an object. Keep it in a variable.

requirements.title: Both logged
requirements.description: Calls console.log to print the restored object. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Print a number from the restored object plus one, and print a property of the original.

requirements.title: restored is a separate object rebuilt from the saved text
requirements.description: saved is a string, and restored is a different object holding the same data as player. Help: 3.8.9 (A Round Trip)
requirements.hint: Do the full trip: saved = JSON.stringify(player), then restored = JSON.parse(saved). Changing a number of restored afterwards (restored.score++) is fine; restored = player is not a copy.

checks.expr: typeof saved === 'string' && restored !== null && typeof restored === 'object' && JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(saved)) === JSON.stringify(player) && JSON.stringify(Object.keys(restored)) === JSON.stringify(Object.keys(player).filter(($k) => typeof player[$k] !== 'function' && player[$k] !== undefined)) && Object.keys(restored).every(($k) => typeof player[$k] === 'number' ? typeof restored[$k] === 'number' : JSON.stringify(restored[$k]) === JSON.stringify(player[$k])) && Object.keys(player).length >= 2 && !same('restored', 'player')
checks.fail: saved should be the JSON text of player, and restored an object rebuilt from saved: the same keys and text values as player (changing one of its numbers afterwards is fine).

requirements.title: saved and restored come from player, and the prints come from restored and player
requirements.description: When player holds other values, saved and restored change with it; a console.log that runs prints a number of restored plus one, and another prints one of player's properties. Help: 3.8.9 (A Round Trip)
requirements.hint: Print restored.score + 1 (any number property) and one property of player. Text typed in by hand does not change when player does.

checks.fail: saved has to be the text JSON.stringify makes from player: when the checker changes player, saved must change with it. Text typed in by hand stays the same.
restored has to come from JSON.parse(saved): when the checker changes player, restored must change with it. An object typed in by hand stays the same.
Print a number from restored plus one, console.log(restored.score + 1) (or restored.score++ and then print it), with a console.log that runs. Typed-in text does not count.
Print one of player's own properties too, console.log(player.name), with a console.log that runs.
